A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same xRFM work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original xRFM benchmark results, runtime measurements and synthetic and real-data feature analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds split-method, temperature-tuning, dataset-characteristic and model-portfolio analyses.

M1.justification: v2 routes each prediction to one leaf. v3 Appendix B adds optional temperature-tuned routing that averages predictions from up to eight leaves using products of node weights. Appendix D also introduces validation-based selection among xRFM and GBDTs. These add substantive prediction procedures, while the original leaf learner and Algorithms A.1–A.5 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The three benchmark suites and interpretability tasks remain. New Table E.2 includes Diabetes130US and KDDCup99 beyond v2's ten named meta-test classification datasets. However, v2 does not enumerate its 300 TALENT datasets, so whether these introduce new underlying data or reuse previously evaluated coverage cannot be established.

E2.justification: Tables E.1–E.2 add explicit comparisons of AGOP, AGOP+TT, PCA+TT and RF+TT splitting variants. Table E.3 adds an original-RFM comparison on large TALENT classification datasets, and E.17 compares validation-selected portfolios. The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; TabDPT was already present in v2.

E3.justification: The new split study uses a 40,000-sample split threshold and validation tuning over hard routing plus 15 temperatures. The portfolio evaluation introduces validation-based model selection on 200 datasets with available validation results. These are additional protocols; the existing benchmark search spaces, including the 60,000-sample threshold, are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative split-method and temperature ablations, including runtime tradeoffs (E.1–E.2), a large-dataset RFM comparison (E.3), benchmark-overlap analyses (E.14–E.16), portfolio analyses (E.17), and performance versus dataset metafeatures (F.3). These substantially expand investigation of the method's design and behavior beyond v2's benchmark and interpretability evidence.

E5.justification: Table E.13 newly reports asymmetric Elo uncertainty bounds, whereas v2's corresponding table contains point estimates only. Their confidence level and estimation procedure are unspecified. The existing Wilcoxon comparison and five-split averaging for the retained meta-test results remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v2's binary TabArena Table B.10 duplicates its regression Table B.8; v3 replaces it with distinct binary results in E.13, including xRFM (T) Elo 1251 instead of 1504. This is a reporting correction. Numerous supplementary results are also added, while matched TALENT, original meta-test, and TabArena regression/multiclass tables retain their values.

T1.justification: Appendix B introduces mathematical definitions for temperature-scaled sigmoid node weights and path-product leaf weights, relating hard routing to zero temperature. Existing kernel, AGOP and metric definitions remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: strong tabular prediction, scalable tree-based local feature learning, and native AGOP interpretability. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains how globally simple targets or poor splits can make partitioning harmful and discusses the cost of leaf ensembling. Appendix C considers tuning, cross-validation, baselines and metrics as possible explanations for benchmark differences after examining dataset overlap. Existing AGOP interpretations and principal future-work discussions remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies temperature-grid limits of 0.025–4.5, the eight-leaf ensemble cap, and supplementary split settings. A.3 also documents 50 sampled configurations and coordinate standardization for TabPFN-v2 embedding experiments, although corresponding outcomes are not reported. Existing implementation descriptions, main search spaces and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and principal positioning relative to RFMs, scalable kernels, GBDTs and tabular foundation models remain unchanged. Switching from numbered to author-year citations does not add related work.

P1.justification: Main section order and most prose remain intact. v3 expands selected results paragraphs, introduces focused appendix sections B–D and F, and updates author affiliations, acknowledgments, headers and citation style. These are localized editorial and organizational changes.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from six to nine panels, adding normalized-error versus training-time plots. Seven supplementary tables and Figures F.1 and F.3 are added; existing tables and figures are redistributed under the ICLR layout. The original runtime Figure B.1 is retained as F.2, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important evidential and reporting weaknesses: it quantifies split-design alternatives and their computational costs, investigates benchmark dependence, and replaces the duplicated binary TabArena table with task-specific results and uncertainty bounds. These substantially improve support and auditability while preserving the main benchmark evidence. The added tables also expose increased routing costs and nonuniform portfolio gains, although uncertainty-estimation details remain sparse.
